title: Old Chapel Road Rising
premise: Folklorist Zephyrine Iversen arrives in the dying village of Hollowmere to record its last songs, but every tune she captures vanishes from her tapes by morning. When an excavation crew unearths a chapel door sealed from the inside, the village's oldest family begins signing away their land one signature at a time — and each signature feeds something beneath Old Chapel Road that is counting down to a final resident. Zephyrine, who has never believed in anything, must choose between her duty to document and her growing love for Wren, the last heir, and get the family out before the count reaches one. In the end she burns her recordings, signs nothing, and walks out with Wren as the door seals itself again — this time from the outside.
about_author: Tamsin Zhou is a former archivist of oral histories who spent three years collecting songs in remote coastal villages before turning to fiction. She writes horror rooted in folklore, drawn to stories where belief is less dangerous than doubt.

chapters.title: The Songs They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Iversen arrives in Hollowmere with recording equipment and professional skepticism, interviewing villagers who hum fragments of songs but refuse to repeat them. Her landlady, Maren, sings one verse of a lullaby and goes pale when asked for the second. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: What the Excavation Turned Up
chapters.summary: A county crew digging a drainage trench strikes old masonry: a chapel door, oak and iron, sealed shut from the inside. The foreman jokes about it; the workers won't touch it after dark. Zephyrine photographs it and finds her camera has recorded forty extra frames she never took. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: rational explanations beginning to strain.

chapters.title: The Iversen Papers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine discovers her own surname in parish records — an ancestor who witnessed the original sealing two centuries ago. The village elders treat her arrival as expected, even scheduled. Maren warns her gently to leave before the papers come around. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering you were summoned.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Zephyrine meets Wren Aldous, last heir of the family that owns everything above the buried door, sharp-tongued and desperate to sell the land and leave. Their first real conversation happens over the vanished tape of the lullaby, which plays back empty except for breathing. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: reluctant connection; love beginning against her better judgment.

chapters.title: First Signature
chapters.summary: A lawyer arrives with documents no one ordered; Wren's uncle signs away the eastern fields and that night stops speaking entirely, his mouth moving in silent song. The count, whatever counts, has begun. Zephyrine's recordings now play sounds from inside the door. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: dread becoming concrete.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Zephyrine pieces together the pattern from parish ledgers: each signature diminishes the household, and when the last resident signs, the door opens from within. The village knows; they've done this arithmetic before. She tries to convince Wren, who thinks she's losing her mind. POV: alternating Zephyrine and Wren. Emotional beat: duty versus denial.

chapters.title: Second Verse
chapters.summary: Maren finally sings the lullaby whole: it is a counting song, a lullaby sung to keep the thing asleep, and the verses have been dropping out of memory for generations. Zephyrine realizes her recordings are the only complete version left — and the thing below wants them sung aloud. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: terrible understanding; the folklorist's archive becomes a weapon aimed at her.

chapters.title: What the Door Wants Signed
chapters.summary: The lawyer returns for Wren's signature; pressure mounts as neighbors turn strange and the road itself seems to lengthen toward the chapel. Zephyrine and Wren admit what they mean to each other in the shadow of the sealed door, which is warm to the touch. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: love declared against duty; resolve forming.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren is brought to sign at midnight on Old Chapel Road; Zephyrine plays the complete lullaby through the door's keyhole, waking rather than soothing what sleeps, forcing the count to break mid-number. The signatures burn, the lawyer unravels into paper, and the door groans open onto darkness that Zephyrine refuses to look at. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: sacrifice, terror, defiance.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Outside
chapters.summary: Resolution. The surviving family leaves Hollowmere at dawn; Zephyrine burns her tapes and her notes, keeping only one photograph of the door. She and Wren drive out as the village behind them grows quiet in a way that feels like sleep. On the radio, faintly, someone hums the second verse. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief, relief, and the cost of believing at last.
